dek: Addresses, hours and what to know before you walk into 8 Manhattan lounges.

slides.label: The Map
slides.text: Six of Manhattan's *eight* best hookah lounges sit blocks apart in the *East Village*.

slides.label: Kazuza
slides.text: *Kazuza* on Avenue A: about 50 flavors, happy hour 4 to 7 PM, open till 4 AM, belly dancer Fri/Sat.

slides.label: Horus Cafe
slides.text: *Horus Cafe* has held its Avenue B corner for well over a decade. Hours unconfirmed, so call first.

slides.label: Eastside Story
slides.text: *Eastside Story* serves no alcohol, just a smooth draw, a back room and a backyard to slow down in.

slides.label: Cozy & La Sultana
slides.text: *Cozy Cafe* runs cheaper with free coal changes. *La Sultana* is cash only, three smokers per hookah max.

slides.label: Sahara East
slides.text: *Sahara East* opens earliest, at noon, and smokes outdoors year round in a heated tent.

slides.label: LES & Murray Hill
slides.text: LES: *Mazaar Lounge* spins hip hop and reggae. Murray Hill: *Mira Mediterranean*, the priciest room, business casual only.

slides.label: The Fine Print
slides.text: Hookah is a *vibe, not a vitamin*. Water cools smoke, it doesn't clean it, so pace your session.

Looking for the best hookah lounges in Manhattan? Here are the 8 rooms worth the trip, from Avenue A to Murray Hill.

Six of the eight sit blocks apart in the East Village: Kazuza's 50 flavors and Friday night belly dancer, Eastside Story's alcohol free back room, Cozy Cafe's cheap coal changes, La Sultana's cash only speakeasy calm, and Sahara East's heated outdoor tent.

On the Lower East Side, Mazaar Lounge spins old school hip hop and reggae. In Murray Hill, Mira Mediterranean brings dinner, cocktails and premium hookah from Champion Pizza's founder, the priciest room on this list.

caption_linkedin:
The best hookah lounges in Manhattan tell a small business story worth noticing.

Most of the East Village rooms on our list run on thin margins and loyal regulars, Cozy Cafe keeps costs down with free coal changes, La Sultana stays cash only and caps each hookah at three people to protect the vibe.

Then there is Mira Mediterranean in Murray Hill, the priciest room on the list, opened by Hakki Akdeniz, the founder of Champion Pizza. It pairs dinner, cocktails and premium hookah under one roof, and much of its best in NYC press is sponsored, worth remembering before you let a headline pick your spot.

Two different playbooks, same city, same industry. Which approach would you bet on for longevity, volume and loyalty, or price and polish? #SmallBusiness #NYC #HospitalityIndustry
